about.title: About us
about.heroText: LidoRank is an independent civic project: bringing transparency to beaches worldwide with structured reviews and verifiable data, useful to citizens and to the authorities overseeing the maritime public domain.
about.giorgioBio: Italian engineer specialized in advanced artificial-intelligence systems for the aerospace and defense sector. He holds a BSc in Computer Science and an MSc in Artificial Intelligence (with honors) from Northeastern University London, and has collaborated with DESY researchers on quantum convolutional neural networks. His interests go beyond engineering, touching the social implications of AI — economics, political philosophy, the history of technological change. He is the author of the book AMAKOM: A Perpetual Peace for the Age of Robots.
about.francescoBio: Italian Ph.D. researcher in Political Science and International Relations at the University of Southern California, specializing in comparative politics, international relations, and analytical political theory. His research examines the implementation and local consequences of the Bolkestein Directive, focusing more broadly on how local social capital shapes community and institutional responses to market-liberalization policies within the European integration process. Drawing on fieldwork with public officials, beach operators, and beachgoers, he studies strategies of harmonization, adaptation, and institutional change. A native of Livorno, Francesco holds an MA in Legal and Political Theory from University College London and a BA in Economics and Finance from the University of Pisa.
about.p1: LidoRank started from a simple question: why is choosing a beach club still so opaque? Prices not always posted, sea access that should be free by law, family services and accessibility hard to compare. In the middle of the debate on concessions (the Bolkestein Directive), a neutral tool was missing.
about.p2: The idea is to combine two worlds: the rigor of public data (maritime-domain concessions) and the real experience of people (vertical reviews across nine criteria). An information base useful to citizens for choosing and to authorities for oversight.
about.p3: LidoRank was co-founded by Giorgio Menicagli Pirina and Francesco Mancuso. Giorgio leads product and engineering; Francesco leads policy analysis, research and institutional relations. Built also with the help of artificial-intelligence tools, under human supervision.

methodology.title: How the rankings work
methodology.intro: Transparency first: here's how LidoRank's scores and rankings are built, and why a ranking is sometimes shown as “in progress”.
methodology.s1Body: Every score comes from someone filling in the questionnaire across our nine criteria. We keep three categories clearly distinct: anonymous review; verified-account review (we verify the writer's email address, not the individual visit); and — in the future — verified visit. We do not solicit or publish fake or paid reviews, and when we detect manipulation we act as explained below.
methodology.s2Title: A weighted score, not a plain average
methodology.s2Body: A ranking score isn't the plain average of the votes: we use a Bayesian weighted average. We start from a cautious baseline equal to the overall mean of all reviews published on the platform, with a weight equivalent to about 8 reviews: with few votes the score stays close to this mean, and as reviews grow it increasingly reflects the club's real judgement. This way a club with a single enthusiastic review doesn't leapfrog one with dozens of solid ones.
methodology.s3Body: A club enters a ranking only after a minimum number of reviews: at least {comune} for the town ranking, {regione} for the regional one and {nazionale} for the national one. Below these thresholds we assign no position: we'd rather say “ranking in progress” than crown a “best” on the basis of very little data. The position shown (#1, #2…) is computed only among clubs that have passed the threshold.
methodology.s4Title: How much a review counts, and anti-fraud defences
methodology.s4Body: Not all reviews count the same. A verified-account review carries full weight; an anonymous one counts about a quarter: it stays visible but moves the score less. A review that is quarantined or rejected drops out of the calculation entirely (zero weight) while remaining on record. On top of this, rate limits and an anti-surge damper temporarily hold suspicious spikes. We don't publish the exact anti-fraud parameters here, as that would make them easier to game.
methodology.s5Title: User-reported information, kept separate from ratings
methodology.s5Body: On the profile we keep subjective ratings (your experience) separate from the factual information users report (sea access, showers, deposit chip). The latter is shown as aggregate percentages, is made up of reviewers' statements rather than findings by LidoRank or any authority, and does not, on its own, turn a club into “non-compliant”: any reports of violations follow a separate, private path.
methodology.disclaimer: LidoRank is a pilot-stage platform: thresholds and criteria may be refined as the community grows.
